quick.summary: Why one update for everyone gets ignored, and three questions to tailor it.
quick.takeaway: What they decide, how often, which channel.

beats.line: I send everyone the same weekly update. Why does the director never read it?
Does she need everything in it?
Probably just whether we’re on track.
People need different things, at different times.
Ask three things about each person. First, what do they decide?
How often? Some want weekly, some only when something changes.
And how? A quick message, a meeting, or a written note.
That sounds like a lot of extra work.
Less than writing an update nobody reads.
Director: on track or not, by message, every Friday.
Two lines she’ll read, instead of two pages she won’t.

quiz.question: What should decide what goes in an update for a senior stakeholder?
options: Everything the team did that week
The length of last week’s update
quiz.explanation: An update earns attention when it serves the decisions that person makes.

quiz.question: Sending everyone the same detailed update is the best way to keep people informed.
quiz.explanation: Different people decide different things. Tailoring what, how often and which channel gets updates read.
